title: Research notes: Treaty of Fort McIntosh, 1785
summary: Sources for the January 21, 1785 treaty with the Wyandot, Delaware, Ojibwe and Odawa. Out-of-state (Beaver, Pennsylvania), so the story has no map pin.

items.text: Signed January 21, 1785 at Fort McIntosh (Beaver, Pa.); ten articles; commissioners George Rogers Clark, Richard Butler, Arthur Lee.
Article I: three chiefs (one Wyandot, two Delaware) held as hostages until prisoners “white and black” are restored.

Articles III–VI: boundary from the Cuyahoga to the Tuscarawas, Fort Laurens, Pickawillany portage, Great Miami (Maumee) and Lake Erie; land inside allotted to the Wyandot and Delaware; settlers there lose U.S. protection; land outside acknowledged as American.
Most signers lacked authority from their nations; later chiefs questioned its legality.

Most Ohio Country nations rejected it, especially the Shawnee, who lost their southwestern Ohio lands; it led to the Western (Northwestern) Confederacy later in 1785 and foreshadowed the Northwest Indian War.
Greenville (1795) drew an almost identical line.
Fort built 1778, named for Gen. Lachlan McIntosh; NRHP 1975.

timeline.event: Treaty of Fort Stanwix with the Six Nations.
